implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py → add_tx(tracker, "expense") calls tracker.add_transaction(...) with tx_type "expense"
main.py → add_tx(tracker, "income") calls tracker.add_transaction(...) with tx_type "income"
main.py → show_txs(tracker) iterates over tracker.transactions and prints each
main.py → delete_tx(tracker) uses tracker.remove_transaction(tid) and reports result
main.py → show_budgets(tracker) uses tracker.budget_status() to display limits, spent, remaining
main.py → show_summary(tracker) prints totals from tracker.totals() and progress from tracker.savings_progress()

implemented_requirements.requirement: Monthly report (income, expenses, net, per‑category breakdown)
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py → show_report(tracker) calls tracker.monthly_report(month) and tracker.category_expenses(rows)
storage.py provides load_data() / save_data(); main.py loads at start and saves on exit via tracker.persist()

judge.summary: The repository contains a complete, runnable CLI budget tracker. All core functionalities—recording expenses/income, listing and deleting transactions, setting per‑category budgets, defining a savings goal, displaying summary/progress, and generating monthly reports—are implemented with concrete code. Data persistence is handled via JSON storage. No major bugs or missing core features are evident, so the submission meets the benchmark.
